mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite sustained FEDFUNDS > 4% for 6 months, or IC > 0.05 over a 12-month horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 2% AND UNRATE < prev(UNRATE) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day rolling returns over the 60-day horizon are negative, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE changes and SPX returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102 suggests weakening manufacturing demand, which lowers corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO remaining below 102 for 6 months, or IC > 0.2 over the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain higher rates, which reduces the present value of equities and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative when CPIAUCSL surprise > +0.3%, or IC < 0.05 over the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining residential mortgage applications (not in the catalog, so skip to alternative) — instead: A sustained decline in the GDP deflator (not in the catalog) — instead: A sustained decline in the S&P 500 itself as a proxy for market pessimism, when combined with rising FEDFUNDS, amplifies downward pressure on future earnings expectations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: market pessimism combined with rising rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite 6 months of FEDFUNDS > 4% and GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5% for the first time in three months, it often precedes a labor market tightening that raises wage growth expectations, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% AND prev(UNRATE) >= 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE crossing below 5% as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month drop in retail sales (not in the catalog) — instead: A 3-month decline in the S&P 500's own monthly returns as a proxy for valuations, coupled with a rise in FEDFUNDS, indicates a supply-side constraint in credit availability, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when FEDFUNDS rises and GDPC1 declines, contradicting the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL vintage < 237.5) and rising FEDFUNDS, the immediate 5-day S&P 500 forward return is negatively impacted due to the Fed's anticipation of further rate hikes, even if short-term economic data are positive.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 237.5 AND FEDFUNDS > previous(FEDFUNDS) for the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when CPIAUCSL is below 237.5 and FEDFUNDS rises, indicating the regime assumption was incorrect.
